species.look_here_first: Start with the long naked flower stalk and perfume. Fragrant gaillardia is a taprooted perennial with a basal rosette, very long mostly leafless peduncles, fragrant heads, and rays that may be tiny or completely absent, leaving a pincushion-like purple-brown disk.

species.look_here_first: Look BELOW EACH HEAD for a second, obvious ARMOR COLLAR: a ring of spiny-margined leaflike bracts about as long as the 30–50 mm involucre. Those are separate SUBTENDING BRACTS, not the individual phyllaries of the involucre. Leaves often bear stout main marginal spines (5–30 mm, variable by variety) and cauline leaf bases may be auriculate-clasping. Color varies white/yellow/pink/purple—yellow thistle is not necessarily yellow. Compared with C. vulgare check the UPPER LEAF BLADE for bristle-spines, not just rough marginal prickles.
